# Workloads API

Manage applications and runtimes. Build and deploy actions can consume paid resources; use a disposable workload when trying examples. Set workload_image to an image or rootfs supported by your deployment configuration and region to an available region from Get deployment context.

Use [API authentication](authentication.md) for protected requests. Examples use your own resource IDs and a temporary token; saved response examples are synthetic.

| Method | Path | Operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload` | [List workloads](#op-get-v1-workload) |
| `POST` | `/v1/workload` | [Create workload](#op-post-v1-workload) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload/{id}` | [Get workload](#op-get-v1-workload-id) |
| `PUT` | `/v1/workload/{id}` | [Update workload](#op-put-v1-workload-id) |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/workload/{id}` | [Delete workload](#op-delete-v1-workload-id) |
| `POST` | `/v1/workload/{id}/build` | [Build workload from repository](#op-post-v1-workload-id-build) |
| `POST` | `/v1/workload/{id}/deploy` | [Deploy workload](#op-post-v1-workload-id-deploy) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload/{id}/builds` | [List workload builds](#op-get-v1-workload-id-builds) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload/{id}/builds/{build_id}/logs` | [Get build logs](#op-get-v1-workload-id-builds-build-id-logs) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload/{id}/logs` | [Get workload logs](#op-get-v1-workload-id-logs) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload/{id}/replicas` | [List workload replicas](#op-get-v1-workload-id-replicas) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload/{id}/runtime-status` | [Get workload runtime status](#op-get-v1-workload-id-runtime-status) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workload/{id}/runtime-notices` | [Get workload runtime notices](#op-get-v1-workload-id-runtime-notices) |

## List workloads {#op-get-v1-workload}

`GET /v1/workload`

Returns a paginated list of Workload

Authentication: bearer token and the team header shown below.

### Parameters

| Name | Location | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | header | yes | Active team ID. Must match the tenant bound to a diagnostic token. |
| `page` | query | no | Page number |
| `per_page` | query | no | Items per page |

### Request example

Set `ADIOS_API_URL=https://api.adios.dev`. For protected requests, set `ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ADIOS_TEAM_ID` as in the [quickstart](quickstart.md). Set any additional `ADIOS_*` variables from your own resource results.

```sh
curl --fail-with-body --request GET "$ADIOS_API_URL/v1/workload" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: $ADIOS_TEAM_ID"
```


### Response: HTTP 200

List of Workload

### Response fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | array |  |
| `data[].allow_default_domain` | boolean | Whether to allow access via the default \*.adios.run domain when a custom domain is configured |
| `data[].branch` | string | Git branch or tag |
| `data[].build_id` | string | Link to specific build artifact |
| `data[].config` | object | Workload specific configuration (e.g. cron schedule, queue name, db user) |
| `data[].created_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].current_source_artifact_id` | string | API source artifact record for the currently deployed build |
| `data[].deleted_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].domain` | string | Generated \*.adios.run hostname or a verified user-owned custom domain; \*.adios.dev and custom \*.adios.run assignments are reserved |
| `data[].env_vars` | object |  |
| `data[].image` | string | Docker image or rootfs location |
| `data[].name` | string |  |
| `data[].node_id` | string |  |
| `data[].parent_id` | string |  |
| `data[].port` | integer | Network port the workload listens on |
| `data[].region` | string |  |
| `data[].repository_url` | string | Git repository URL |
| `data[].requires` | object | List of required capabilities or services |
| `data[].resources` | object | Resource requirements (cpu, ram, disk) |
| `data[].status` | string |  |
| `data[].team_id` | string |  |
| `data[].template` | string | Template name and version (e.g. postgres:16) |
| `data[].type` | string |  Allowed: app, api, worker, function, cron, queue, database, cache. |
| `data[].updated_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].variant` | string |  |
| `data[].version` | string | Semantic version or commit hash |
| `data[].volumes` | object | List of volume mounts |
| `data[].workload_id` | string |  |
| `pagination` | object |  |
| `pagination.page` | integer | Current page number |
| `pagination.per_page` | integer | Number of items per page |
| `pagination.total` | integer | Total number of items |

Illustrative example; not a live response:

```json
    {
```

## Build workload from repository {#op-post-v1-workload-id-build}

`POST /v1/workload/{id}/build`

Build the workload using its configured repository. Set repository_url on the workload first, or enable repo here. A paid subscription may be required.

Set `workload_id` using IDs from your own API responses.

This request changes data or starts an action. Review the target and body before sending it.

Authentication: bearer token and the team header shown below.

### Parameters

| Name | Location | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | Resource identifier from your team's API results. |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | header | yes | Active team ID. Must match the tenant bound to a diagnostic token. |
| `repo` | query | no | Override the configured Git repository. |
| `branch` | query | no | Override the repository branch. |
| `async` | query | no | Return while the build runs in the background. |

### Request example

Set `ADIOS_API_URL=https://api.adios.dev`. For protected requests, set `ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ADIOS_TEAM_ID` as in the [quickstart](quickstart.md). Set any additional `ADIOS_*` variables from your own resource results.

```sh
curl --fail-with-body --request POST "$ADIOS_API_URL/v1/workload/${ADIOS_WORKLOAD_ID}/build?async=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: $ADIOS_TEAM_ID"
```


### Response: HTTP 200

Successful response. Inspect returned state for operations that start asynchronous work.

A complete response-body schema is not published for this custom operation. Inspect the returned content and status; no payload is assumed here.

## Deploy workload {#op-post-v1-workload-id-deploy}

`POST /v1/workload/{id}/deploy`

Build and deploy from the configured repository or deploy an existing build_id. This changes the running workload and may incur usage charges.

Set `workload_id` using IDs from your own API responses.

This request changes data or starts an action. Review the target and body before sending it.

Authentication: bearer token and the team header shown below.

### Parameters

| Name | Location | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | Resource identifier from your team's API results. |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | header | yes | Active team ID. Must match the tenant bound to a diagnostic token. |
| `build_id` | query | no | Deploy a previously built artifact. |
| `region` | query | no | Override the deployment region. |

Set `ADIOS_API_URL=https://api.adios.dev`. For protected requests, set `ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ADIOS_TEAM_ID` as in the [quickstart](quickstart.md). Set any additional `ADIOS_*` variables from your own resource results.

```sh

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
```
